a11yFix_missing-label: Set contentDescription (Android) or accessibilityLabel (iOS) to the action, e.g. “Close”.
a11yFix_touch-target: Grow the tappable area with padding or minHeight/minWidth; the icon itself can stay small.
a11yFix_duplicate-label: Make each label say what it acts on: “Delete card *1234” instead of “Delete”.
a11yFix_low-contrast: Darken the text or lighten the background until the ratio reaches the requirement.
a11yFix_input-without-label: Give the field a visible label linked to it (labelFor / accessibilityLabel).
a11yFix_redundant-role: Remove “button”, “icon”, “image” from the label: the platform announces the role.
a11yFix_not-accessible: Set isAccessibilityElement = true on the control or its container.
a11yFix_non-text-contrast: Use a darker icon or outline, at least 3 : 1 against what is behind it.
a11yFix_target-spacing: Enlarge the targets or add space between them.
a11yFix_nested-clickable: Make either the row or the inner control clickable, or give the inner one a custom action.
a11yFix_hidden-focusable: Hide the element from accessibility while it is invisible (accessibilityElementsHidden / isAccessibilityElement = false).
a11yFix_non-descriptive-label: Write the label as a person would say it: “Share”, not “shareButton”.
a11yFix_hint-only-input: Add a persistent label above the field and keep the hint for an example value.
a11yFix_state-missing: Use a real Switch/CheckBox or expose the state (stateDescription / accessibilityValue).
a11yFix_text-clipping: Let the text wrap to more lines, or shorten it; check again with the largest font.
a11yFix_reading-order: Order the views in the layout as they appear, or set accessibilityTraversalBefore/After.

finding_android-allow-backup_why: With allowBackup on, tokens and databases of the app can be copied off the phone with adb backup or a cloud backup.
finding_android-allow-backup_fix: Set android:allowBackup="false", or limit what is backed up with dataExtractionRules / fullBackupContent.
finding_android-debuggable_why: Anyone with the phone can attach a debugger and read the app's memory and files. Fine for a test build, never for a release.
finding_android-debuggable_fix: Make sure the release build type has debuggable false.
finding_android-cleartext_why: usesCleartextTraffic lets the app send data without encryption, which anyone on the network can read.
finding_android-cleartext_fix: Remove usesCleartextTraffic="true"; allow HTTP for specific test hosts in network_security_config only.
finding_android-exported_why: An exported component without a permission can be called by any app on the phone, bypassing the app's own screens and checks.
finding_android-exported_fix: Set android:exported="false" where other apps do not need it, or protect it with android:permission.
finding_android-dangerous-permissions_wh: {{list}}. Each one needs a reason the store review and the users accept.
finding_android-dangerous-permissions_fi: Remove the permissions the app does not use; check that each one asked at runtime has a clear explanation.
finding_android-target-sdk_why: Google Play refuses updates that target an old Android version, and the app misses newer privacy protections.
finding_android-target-sdk_fix: Raise targetSdkVersion to {{min}} or newer and retest permissions and background work.
finding_android-test-only_title: The APK is marked test only
finding_android-test-only_why: android:testOnly builds install only with adb install -t and cannot go to the store. Usually a build from the IDE's Run button.
finding_android-test-only_fix: Take the build from the CI pipeline instead of the IDE.
finding_ios-ats-arbitrary-loads_why: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads lets the app use plain HTTP and weak TLS everywhere. App Review asks why.
finding_ios-ats-arbitrary-loads_fix: Remove NSAllowsArbitraryLoads; list only the hosts that really need an exception under NSExceptionDomains.
finding_ios-ats-insecure-domain_why: Traffic to these hosts can travel without encryption: {{domain}}.
finding_ios-ats-insecure-domain_fix: Move the hosts to HTTPS and drop NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads.
finding_ios-get-task-allow_why: get-task-allow lets a debugger attach to the app. Development builds have it; App Store and TestFlight builds must not.
finding_ios-get-task-allow_fix: Sign the build for testers with an ad hoc or distribution profile.
finding_ios-file-sharing_title: App files are open in Finder and Files
finding_ios-file-sharing_why: UIFileSharingEnabled shows the app's Documents folder to anyone with the phone and a cable.
finding_ios-file-sharing_fix: Turn file sharing off, or keep sensitive data out of Documents.
finding_ios-url-schemes_why: Any app or web page can open these links. Check that each handler validates its input and asks before acting.
finding_ios-url-schemes_fix: Test every deep link with unexpected and missing parameters; prefer universal links for sensitive actions.
finding_ios-profile-expiring_title: The provisioning profile expires in {{days}} days
finding_ios-profile-expiring_why: When it expires the app stops launching on test devices.
finding_ios-profile-expiring_fix: Renew the profile and rebuild before it runs out.

finding_log-crash_why: An uncaught exception closed the app in front of the user.
finding_log-crash_fix: Open the line for the stack trace and attach it to the bug with the steps that led there.
finding_log-native-crash_why: Native code (C/C++, a library or the WebView) crashed the process.
finding_log-native-crash_fix: Attach the tombstone (adb bugreport) and the steps; the developers need the native stack.
finding_log-anr_why: {{reason}}. The system offered to close the app: the main thread was busy for too long.
finding_log-anr_fix: Note what was on screen and what you tapped; attach the log and /data/anr traces.
finding_log-strict-mode_why: Disk or network work on the main thread makes the interface stutter and can lead to ANRs.
finding_log-strict-mode_fix: Report the screen where it happens; the developers move the work off the main thread.
finding_log-ios-exception_why: An uncaught Objective-C or Swift exception closed the app.
finding_log-ios-exception_fix: Attach the crash report from the device (Settings › Privacy › Analytics) and the steps.

finding_traffic-error_why: The server answered with an error. Check whether the app shows the user something sensible.
finding_traffic-error_fix: Attach the request and the response to the bug; if the error is expected, add it to the expected errors.
finding_traffic-slow_why: {{ms}} ms with a limit of {{limit}} ms. The user waits with a spinner.
finding_traffic-slow_fix: Report it with the timings; if the endpoint is slow by nature, give it its own limit.
finding_traffic-duplicate_why: The same request went {{count}} times within {{windowMs}} ms: extra load and battery, sometimes double actions.
finding_traffic-duplicate_fix: Tell the developers on which screen it happens; polling can be added to the patterns that are not duplicates.

wsAppsError_xcodeTooOld: Xcode {{xcode}} cannot work with iOS {{ios}} on this iPhone: update Xcode. Until then apps, sessions and installs on it will not work.
wsAppsError_deviceLocked: Unlock the iPhone and trust this computer, then refresh.
wsAppsError_notPaired: The iPhone is not paired with this Mac: unlock it and tap Trust.
wsAppsError_failed: Could not read the apps on the device.
quickSigningNoTeam: A real iPhone needs WebDriverAgent signed, and this Mac has no development certificate. Add an Apple ID in Xcode → Settings → Accounts and create an Apple Development certificate.
quickSigningPickTeam: This Mac has {{count}} development teams. Pick the one to sign WebDriverAgent with.
settingsDevicesText: What sessions on real devices need.
settingsIosPurpose: Appium puts its WebDriverAgent app on a real iPhone, and Xcode has to sign it with a development certificate
settingsIosNoTeam: This Mac has no development certificate
settingsIosNoTeamHow: Xcode → Settings → Accounts → “+” → Apple ID (work or personal). Then Manage Certificates → “+” → Apple Development. Then press “Look again”.
settingsIosPick: There are several teams: pick the one your iPhone is registered with.
settingsIosBundleIdHint: Empty: the team’s own ID. Change it if your team already has a profile for WebDriverAgent.
settingsIosPhoneSteps: On the iPhone: turn on Developer Mode (Settings → Privacy & Security), unlock it and trust this Mac. With a personal team, after the first start allow the developer in Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.
sessionHintWdaTitle: WebDriverAgent did not start on the iPhone
sessionHintWdaText: Xcode could not build or sign WebDriverAgent. Check the development team in Settings → Devices, that your Xcode supports the phone’s iOS version, and that the iPhone has Developer Mode on, is unlocked and trusts this Mac. The first build takes a few minutes.
sessionHintNoActivityTitle: The app does not start on the device
sessionHintNoActivityText: The device does not have this app, or it cannot be opened from the launcher. Pick an app installed on this device at the top.
aiDailyLimitHint: Nothing more is sent in a day, so the quota is not used up.
aiConsentSwitchHint: Without it the AI check sends nothing and asks you first.
logsScopeNoAppHint: Pick an app at the top to see only its lines
logsSearchError: The regular expression has an error: {{error}}
logsAppNone: No app picked: the whole device is shown
buildsPipelinePlaceholder: A GitLab pipeline or job link (or just ⌘V on this page)
buildsPipelineBadLink: This is not a GitLab pipeline or job link
buildsPipelineChooseJobs: Which jobs of {{project}} make the build? Tick them: this is kept for the project, in order of preference.
buildsPipelineWaiting: Waiting for {{job}}: {{status}}. Asking GitLab every 10 s.
buildsPipelineManual: Job {{job}} waits to be started by hand
buildsPipelineChooseBuild: The archive has several builds. Pick one; next time the same kind is taken:
buildsPipelineNoJobs: The pipeline has none of the jobs to take the build from. Change the jobs below.
buildsPipelineNoArtifacts: Job {{job}} finished without a build in its artifacts
buildsPipelineRetry: GitLab did not answer: {{error}}. Trying again.
buildsPipelineAuto: Install as soon as it is ready
buildsPipelineError_notSetUp: GitLab is not set up yet: add the site and a token in Settings
buildsPipelineError_otherSite: The link is to another GitLab than the one set up: change the site in Settings
buildsPipelineError_notFound: The pipeline is not there, or the token cannot see it
